query: For high-entropy-alloy materials intended for self-lubricating moving components, what single intervention could reduce both coefficient of friction and wear rate across a wide service-temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the untreated alloy, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites prior evidence supporting it, and proposes an experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Dispersing ~5 vol % CaF₂ nanoparticles throughout a powder-metallurgy Co–Cr–Fe–Ni–Mo₀.₂ high-entropy alloy (HEA) will in situ generate a continuous CaF₂-rich tribofilm during sliding, lowering both the steady‐state dry-air coefficient of friction and the specific wear rate by ≥30 % and ≥50 %, respectively, relative to the nanoparticle-free HEA, from 25 °C up to at least 600 °C.
generation.material_initial_state: Gas-atomised CoCrFeNiMo₀.₂ HEA powder, hot-isostatically pressed and annealed to a single-phase FCC microstructure with ~20 µm grains; no intentional solid-lubricant phases present.
generation.intervention: Introduce 5 vol % CaF₂ nanoparticles (≈100 nm) into the HEA powder prior to consolidation, followed by spark-plasma sintering at 1000 °C/10 min under 50 MPa to create a bulk HEA-CaF₂ nanocomposite.
generation.conditions: Unlubricated, reciprocating sliding against an alumina counterface in dry air at 25 °C, 200 °C, 400 °C, and 600 °C, 5 N load (≈1 GPa Hertzian contact pressure), 5 Hz, 5 mm stroke length.
generation.structural_mediator: Uniformly dispersed, thermally stable CaF₂ nanoparticles located at grain boundaries and triple junctions that can be mechanically extruded to the surface during sliding.
generation.mechanism: Under contact stress and frictional heating, CaF₂ particles soften (≈350 °C transition) and smear onto the wear track, forming a thin, adherent, low-shear-strength CaF₂ tribofilm. This film (i) reduces interfacial shear, lowering friction, and (ii) acts as a sacrificial, load-bearing layer that limits direct metallic asperity contact and adhesive transfer, thereby reducing wear. CaF₂’s wide stability window (−40 °C to ~800 °C) maintains film integrity over the specified temperature range.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared with the untreated HEA, the nanocomposite will show: • Average steady-state COF ≤0.45 vs. ≈0.70 for the baseline (≥30 % reduction). • Specific wear rate ≤3 × 10⁻⁵ mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹ vs. ≈6 × 10⁻⁵ mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹ for the baseline (≥50 % reduction) across all test temperatures.
generation.baseline: Identical CoCrFeNiMo₀.₂ HEA fabricated and tested under the same conditions but without CaF₂ addition.
generation.boundary: Effectiveness expected for 1) temperatures between 25 °C and 600 °C; below 0 °C CaF₂ brittleness may limit film formation, above 800 °C sublimation may occur. 2) Dry or mildly humid air; in water-lubricated or highly humid environments CaF₂ film may dissolve. 3) Contact pressures ≤1.5 GPa; excessive loads could spall the tribofilm.
generation.uncertainty: Potential agglomeration of CaF₂ during sintering could hinder uniform film formation; interfacial reactions between CaF₂ and HEA matrix at 1000 °C are insufficiently characterised; predicted quantitative improvements extrapolate from literature on conventional alloys and may differ for HEAs.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two specimens: (A) baseline CoCrFeNiMo₀.₂ HEA and (B) HEA+5 vol % CaF₂ nanocomposite by identical SPS processing. Conduct reciprocating ball-on-disc tests in dry air at 25 °C, 200 °C, 400 °C and 600 °C under the defined load and stroke. Measure friction force continuously; weigh and 3D-scan discs and balls before and after to determine volume loss.
measurements: Specific wear rate (mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹) of both disc and ball
XPS/Raman mapping of wear tracks for CaF₂ presence
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if, at two or more test temperatures, either (i) the nanocomposite’s average steady-state COF is not at least 15 % lower than the baseline OR (ii) its specific wear rate is not at least 25 % lower than the baseline, indicating the intervention does not robustly reduce both friction and wear.
